title: server.py's comment says consensus_edge defaults ON since 2026-08-04; the flag registry sets it False and the live endpoints 503
claimUnderTest: server.py:2686-2693: 'the consensus_edge feature flag ... default **ON** since 2026-08-04 without being able to move a number that was already on screen. Rollback: RISKIT_FEATURE_CONSENSUS_EDGE=0 + restart.'
observed: src/api/feature_flags.py:260 sets "consensus_edge": False under a 20-line comment ending 'Flipping this default back to True requires the gate in scripts/validate_consensus_edge_board.py to pass on a re-run, not a judgement call. See ADR-023.' ADR-023 is titled 'the flag goes back OFF, on the gate that turned it on'. The router-mount comment recorded the ON flip and was never updated for the same-day revert. Live: every gated route 503s feature_disabled.
userImpact: None for the end user (the flag is correctly off). The damage is to maintenance: a developer reading server.py at the router mount — the natural place to look for 'is this feature live?' — concludes the board is shipping, and may debug a 503 as a bug or re-run a validation gate that already failed. It also makes the code comment disagree with the ADR it is meant to implement.

priorFinding.note: The prior registry covers the consensus_edge flag being off (as designed); it does not flag the contradicting server.py comment.

whatWorks: The gate itself is exemplary — ADR-023 reverted a shipped default on a measurement, the 503 body explains WHY in product terms, and /api/consensus-edge/methodology stays 200 so the refusal is inspectable.
rootCause: Two places record the same fact. The router-mount comment was written on the ON flip; the revert changed only the registry.
requiredRepair: Rewrite server.py:2686-2693 to say the flag defaults OFF per ADR-023, or delete the default claim from that comment entirely and point at feature_flags.py. One place should own a default.

title: CLAUDE.md's three payload-size figures are each ~3x low, and the test that supposedly pins them runs on a fixture 71x smaller than production
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md:806-809 — full contract '~4 MB uncompressed'; delta '~1.25 MB uncompressed, and to ~100 KB over the wire'; 'Regression test ... pins the delta shape, byte-size bounds'.
observed: Measured on the live stack: GET /api/data = 11,953,535 b (11.95 MB); POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta = 3,918,195 b (3.92 MB) and 372,690 b gzipped (373 KB). The named test asserts delta_bytes < 55_000 on a synthetic fixture and its own comment repeats 'delta is ~1.25MB vs ~4MB full', so it propagates the wrong figures and could never detect the drift. The RELATIVE claim survives: 3.92/11.79 = 33.2%, i.e. 66.8% smaller, versus the documented '~70% smaller'.
userImpact: A performance decision gets made against the wrong number. CLAUDE.md's own Performance Rules mandate 'eliminate oversized payloads'; an engineer budgeting against '~4 MB' will conclude the contract is already lean and look elsewhere, while the real cost is 11.95 MB uncompressed on every /rankings load. AUDIT_PROTOCOL's own perf evidence file records the same 3x gap independently.

priorFinding.note: The audit harness measured the full-contract number in evidence/perf/api-data-payload-sizes.txt; the delta figures and the test-assurance half are measured here for the first time.

whatWorks: GZipMiddleware is real (server.py:2670) and does the heavy lifting — 11.95 MB → 1.18 MB on the wire. The delta mechanism genuinely works and genuinely saves ~67%.
rootCause: Figures were written once against a smaller board and never re-measured; the only test that mentions bytes runs on a fixture three orders of magnitude smaller, so nothing in CI is coupled to the real number.
requiredRepair: Update the three figures in CLAUDE.md, fix the stale comment in test_source_overrides.py:631, and add a size assertion that runs against a realistic contract (or a CI step that curls the live payload and fails a budget) so the number cannot drift silently again.

title: CLAUDE.md attributes 239 client-numbered rows to the 800-rank limit; the board never reaches 800 and every one of those rows is unpriced
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md:679-681 — 'In practice that is players past the backend's OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800) — rows the backend deliberately left unranked ... This is a display ordinal for otherwise-unnumbered rows, not a ranking engine.'
observed: Measured on the live contract: 1,092 playersArray rows; 740 carry canonicalConsensusRank; the MAXIMUM stamped rank is 740, so no row is anywhere near 800. Of the 352 unranked rows, 113 are picks (correctly suppressed) and 239 are non-picks — and 239 of 239 carry rankDerivedValue = null. They are unranked because the board could not price them, not because they fell past a depth cutoff. buildRows has no value filter, so each of those 239 receives r.rank = computedConsensusRank (an array index) in the # column.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/c.json && python3 -c "import json;pa=json.load(open('/tmp/c.json'))['playersArray'];r=[x for x in pa if isinstance(x.get('canonicalConsensusRank'),int)];u=[x for x in pa if x.get('canonicalConsensusRank') is None and x.get('assetClass')!='pick'];print('rows',len(pa),'ranked',len(r),'maxrank',max(y['canonicalConsensusRank'] for y in r),'unranked_nonpick',len(u),'of_those_null_value',sum(1 for y in u if y.get('rankDerivedValue') is None))"
reproduction.expected: maxrank 800 and unranked rows explained by the limit

userImpact: The doc turns a data-quality gap into a design decision. A reader concludes 'the board is a deliberate top-800 and everything below is intentionally unnumbered', when in fact 239 rows failed to price and are being handed array indices as ranks. That is the difference between 'we stop numbering past 800' and 'we could not value 22% of the pool' — and only the second one prompts anyone to investigate upstream, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md's own 'Fail-fast on missing stamps' paragraph instructs.

priorFinding.note: Independently measured before opening the prior index. PRIOR-A01-F01 measured 216 client-numbered rows on its payload and made the same 800-vs-740 point; I measure 239 unranked non-picks on the 2026-08-04 contract, all with null rankDerivedValue. Same mechanism, same defect, one day of drift in the count. The remediation of the # column belongs to the rankings workstream; the documentation half is filed here.

whatWorks: The suppression logic itself is right: backend stamps always win, picks are never given a client ordinal, and an active valuation overlay suppresses the ordinal entirely (dynasty-data.js:1394-1401). The rule 'no frontend ranking engine' holds for VALUES without exception.
rootCause: The 2026-07-29 correction that added this paragraph explained the mechanism accurately and guessed at the population it applies to, without measuring it.
requiredRepair: Replace the '800' sentence with the measured cause: 'rows the backend could not price (rankDerivedValue null) — 239 of 1,092 on the 2026-08-04 contract'. Then decide separately whether such rows should be numbered at all.
dependencies: Coordinate with the rankings/materializer workstream before changing buildRows.

title: Three in-tree sources give two opposite verdicts on Defect D-2, and CLAUDE.md's is the one that says it is closed
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md:188-190 — 'This resolves Defect D-2 (docs/python-coverage-audit.md), which was open between "503 per this table" and "keep the fallback and fix the doc". Fixing the doc is the answer, and this is it.'
observed: server.py:8270-8271: 'A contract belonging to a *different* league is still served — that is Defect D-2, an open decision, not settled here.' server.py:8303-8305: 'The mismatch case is Defect D-2 in docs/python-coverage-audit.md — an OPEN product decision between "503 per CLAUDE.md's table" and "keep the cross-league fallback and fix the doc".' docs/python-coverage-audit.md:269 heads the section 'D-2 ... *(UNRESOLVED — documented, not fixed)*'. Two of three say open. Separately, the substantive risk that audit flagged is still live: the draft-capital handler (server.py 8255-8420) contains no scoring_profile check at all, while /api/data (server.py:3076) and /api/rankings/overrides (:3817) both 503 on a profile mismatch — so a foreign league on a DIFFERENT scoring profile would be priced from this contract without a guard.

reproduction.command: grep -n 'D-2' CLAUDE.md server.py docs/python-coverage-audit.md; sed -n '8255,8420p' server.py | grep -c scoring_profile
reproduction.expected: one consistent status verb; a profile guard in the handler
reproduction.actual: CLAUDE.md says resolved, server.py x2 and python-coverage-audit.md say open; 0 scoring_profile references in the handler body

numericProof.formula: count of in-tree assertions per verdict

userImpact: Nobody acts on a wrong number today — both live leagues share scoring profile superflex_tep15_ppr1, so the missing guard cannot fire. The cost is that the next person to touch multi-league draft capital reads whichever file they open first and either reopens a closed question or ships against a closed one that the code still treats as open. A third league on a different profile makes it a real defect with no warning.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced verbatim at HEAD, including the sub-claim about the missing scoring_profile guard: the handler range has zero references while /api/data has one.

whatWorks: The D-2 *fix itself* is real and verified: the hardcoded 7000/4000/2000/1200 table is gone (draft_capital_fallback.py:74-79 returns float|None), and a live foreign-league call returns coveredPickYears [2026], pricedPickCount 40, unpricedPickCount 40, unpricedPickYears [2027] on the requested league's own 10-team settings. The mechanism is right; only the status verb and the profile guard are unresolved.
rootCause: CLAUDE.md was edited to close a doc-vs-code disagreement by picking a side, without editing the code comment or the audit doc that hold the other side.
requiredRepair: Adjudicate D-2 once, in one place, and make the other two point at it. If the answer is 'keep the fallback', add the scoring_profile guard so the fallback is safe for the case it was never tested against.

title: meta.sleeperLoadedLeagueKey names the wrong league on a valid cross-league payload, and the documented 503/sleeper-null contract for terminal no longer holds
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md:165-166 'meta.sleeperLoadedLeagueKey — which league the sleeper block *would* be for, when sleeperDataReady: false (diagnostic only)'; :169-172 'serve shared rankings with sleeper: null + sleeperDataReady: false'; :173-176 '/api/terminal, /api/trade/*, /api/angle/* — 503 whenever the loaded contract's leagueKey doesn't match'.
observed: GET /api/data?view=compact&leagueKey=dynasty_new returns sleeperDataReady: TRUE, sleeper NOT null, and sleeper.leagueId 1320092771247222784 / leagueName 'Blood, Sweat, and Beers' / 10 teams — i.e. genuinely the requested league, fetched by the cross-league overlay path at server.py:3240-3263. And yet meta.sleeperLoadedLeagueKey is stamped 'dynasty_main'. The field is set inside the ready=True branch, guarded by `if not sleeper_matches`, so its meaning silently changed from 'which league the sleeper block is' to 'which league the base contract was built for' — the doc still describes the first. GET /api/terminal?leagueKey=dynasty_new returns HTTP 200 with dynasty_new's own teams, not the documented 503; POST /api/trade/finder and /api/angle/find with the same key do 503, so the rule now holds for two of the three families it names.

reproduction.expected: sleeperDataReady false + sleeper null, or sleeperLoadedLeagueKey absent; terminal 503
reproduction.actual: sleeperDataReady true, sleeper present and correct for dynasty_new, sleeperLoadedLeagueKey 'dynasty_main'; terminal 200

numericProof.formula: sleeperLoadedLeagueKey should identify the league whose rosters are in the sleeper block

userImpact: No wrong number reaches a user — the rosters served are the right ones, and the cross-league overlay is genuinely better than the doc describes. The risk is inverted: a diagnostic field that names the wrong league will send whoever debugs a multi-league incident to the wrong league's data, and a developer trusting the 503 table may 'restore' a 503 on /api/terminal and delete working cross-league support to satisfy a doc.

priorFinding.note: The prior registry covers league isolation broadly; the sleeperLoadedLeagueKey mis-stamp on the ready=True overlay branch is measured here.

whatWorks: The cross-league overlay itself is correct and well-built: two different leagues get two different sleeper blocks with the right ids, names and team counts, from one shared scoring-profile contract — exactly what the scoring-profile/leagueKey split promises. The degraded sleeper:null path still exists as the fallback when the overlay fetch fails (server.py:3287-3300).
rootCause: A capability was added (live cross-league roster overlay) that made an existing diagnostic field's name inaccurate, and CLAUDE.md's error table was written for the pre-overlay behaviour.
requiredRepair: Rename the field to what it now means (e.g. contractLeagueKey) or stop stamping it on the ready=True branch; rewrite CLAUDE.md's error table to describe the overlay path as primary and the null path as the fallback, and split /api/terminal out of the trade/angle 503 rule.

title: ADR-001..015 exist in two DECISIONS.md files with unrelated subjects, and 36 of 44 ADR citations in src/ do not say which file
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md:400-403 — 'NOTE: the ADR numbers are per-file, not global — there is a DIFFERENT ADR-008 in docs/league-intelligence/DECISIONS.md about replacement levels. Always cite ADRs with their file'.
observed: The rule is correct and the codebase it governs breaks it. ADR-001 through ADR-015 exist in BOTH docs/league-intelligence/DECISIONS.md and docs/consensus-edge/DECISIONS.md with unrelated subjects — ADR-008 is 'replacement levels use endogenous flex allocation' in one and 'the mispricing component earned its place' in the other; ADR-015 is 'the TE alignment is now a measured basis conversion' versus 'market movement is the right target'. A third file, docs/roster-trade-intelligence/DECISIONS.md, contains exactly one ADR, numbered 008, with no 001-007. Across src/ and server.py there are 44 ADR citations; 36 of them use an id in the ambiguous 001-015 range with no file named, spread over 24 modules including src/bdvm/roster.py ('ADR-004/007'), src/api/gameplan.py ('ADR-011') and src/ros/lineup.py ('ADR-004', 'ADR-007').

reproduction.command: for f in docs/league-intelligence/DECISIONS.md docs/consensus-edge/DECISIONS.md docs/roster-trade-intelligence/DECISIONS.md; do echo "-- $f"; grep -oE '^## ADR-[0-9]+' $f | tr '\n' ' '; echo; done; grep -rnoE 'ADR-0[0-9]{2}' --include=*.py src/ server.py | grep -v __pycache__ | tee /tmp/adr.txt | wc -l; grep -cE 'ADR-0(0[1-9]|1[0-5])$' /tmp/adr.txt
reproduction.expected: one ADR namespace, or every citation file-qualified
reproduction.actual: ADR-001..015 duplicated across two files; 44 citations, 36 ambiguous, 24 modules

numericProof.formula: count of ADR-0NN citations in src/+server.py where NN in 001..015 and no file named

userImpact: No user-facing number moves. The cost lands on anyone trying to change a tuned constant: CLAUDE.md tells you to read the ADR before touching the refit gate, and 36 of the pointers in the code lead to two different documents. In this repo that matters more than usual, because ADRs are where measured decisions (ADR-023 reverting a shipped flag, ADR-015 replacing a flat 1.15 with a measured curve) are recorded — reading the wrong one produces a confidently wrong change.

priorFinding.note: The ambiguity is noted by CLAUDE.md itself; the 36/44 measurement across 24 modules is taken here.

whatWorks: The ADRs are genuinely good — dated, statused, with measurements and explicit supersession (ADR-015 'Supersedes the "no code change yet" half of ADR-009 for Axis A'). The problem is only the namespace.
rootCause: Three subsystems each started their own DECISIONS.md at ADR-001 without a prefix.
requiredRepair: Prefix the ids by subsystem (LI-ADR-008, CE-ADR-008, RTI-ADR-008), keeping the old numbers as aliases in each file's header, then sweep the 36 code citations. Cheap, mechanical, and it makes CLAUDE.md's own rule enforceable by grep.

title: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md tells you to fetch /api/data?view=delta; that route silently ignores the parameter and returns the full 11.95 MB contract
observed: GET /api/data?view=delta returns 11,953,535 bytes — byte-identical to GET /api/data with no view parameter — with payloadView null. It does not call build_rankings_delta_payload. The delta view lives on POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta, which CLAUDE.md:807 documents correctly. Two problems compound: the doc is wrong, AND the route accepts an unrecognised view value silently instead of rejecting it, so the mistake produces no error anywhere — just 3x the bytes.
userImpact: A developer following the architecture doc ships a request they believe is a compact delta and actually transfers 11.95 MB — double even the ?view=app path they would otherwise have used. The silent-accept behaviour means it survives review, CI and production without a single error line. This is the mechanism by which a documentation defect becomes a performance defect.

priorFinding.note: Not present in the prior index.

whatWorks: ?view=app and ?view=compact are real and behave; the POST delta path works and saves 67%.
requiredRepair: Two fixes, both small: correct the ARCHITECTURE.md arrow to POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta, and make /api/data reject an unknown view value with 400 rather than serving the default. The second is what stops the next wrong doc from costing bytes.
rootCause: ARCHITECTURE.md was written from the intent ('the frontend gets a delta') rather than the route; nothing validates the view enum.

title: CLAUDE.md names Selenium as the production scraper's stack twice; no Selenium exists anywhere in the repository
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md:21 'Scraping: Playwright (browser automation), legacy Selenium/requests (Dynasty Scraper.py)' and CLAUDE.md:30 'Dynasty Scraper.py — THE PRODUCTION SCRAPER (Selenium/requests)'.
observed: grep -c selenium 'Dynasty Scraper.py' returns 0, and a repo-wide grep over *.py and *.txt returns no hits at all — including requirements. The file's actual imports are `import requests` (line 52) and `from playwright.async_api import async_playwright` (line 53). The same two sentences also disagree with each other on whether the scraper is legacy: L21 calls it 'legacy', L30-31 says 'Not legacy despite its age'.

reproduction.command: grep -c selenium 'Dynasty Scraper.py'; grep -rln selenium --include=*.py --include=*.txt . | grep -v node_modules; sed -n '52,53p' 'Dynasty Scraper.py'
reproduction.actual: 0 occurrences; no file in the repo mentions selenium; imports are requests + playwright

userImpact: Low but real: the Tech Stack table is the first thing a new contributor reads, and it sends them to install and debug a dependency that is not used. The 'legacy' label is worse than the wrong library — CLAUDE.md's Directory Structure block exists specifically to stop people treating this file as dead code, and the Tech Stack line ten lines earlier undoes it.
whatWorks: The rest of the scraper description is accurate: server.py does import it via importlib, and .github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:14 is cron '42 */2 * * *' — every 2h, exactly as claimed.
rootCause: A stack line written before the Playwright migration, never revisited.
requiredRepair: Replace 'Selenium/requests' with 'Playwright + requests' in both places and drop 'legacy' from L21.

title: Six structural counts in CLAUDE.md are wrong, all in the direction that makes the codebase look smaller than it is
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md's Tech Stack and Directory Structure blocks: 'Next.js 15 + React 19'; 'Next.js app (App Router) — 38 pages'; '28 backend bridge routes'; 'src/ — Modular canonical engine (~250 modules)'; 'exports/ — 141 tracked'; 'data/ — ~7,900 files ARE tracked'.
observed: Measured at HEAD: next 16.2.12 (a full major ahead — bumped by 7b21aba4 on 2026-08-04, after CLAUDE.md's last internal date of 2026-07-31) and react 19.2.8; 41 pages; 36 bridge routes (AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md independently says 36); 300 python modules under src/; 140 tracked files under exports/; 8,198 tracked under data/. README.md:8 repeats the 'Next.js 15' error. Five of six understate. The route count is the exception that proves the point: '~100 routes' is right (openapi reports 99), and it is the only figure written with a tilde.

reproduction.command: grep -E '\"(next|react)\"' frontend/package.json; find frontend/app -name 'page.*' -not -path '*/api/*' | wc -l; find frontend/app/api -name 'route.*' | wc -l; find src -name '*.py' | wc -l; git ls-files exports | wc -l; git ls-files data | wc -l

userImpact: Individually trivial. Collectively they are the measurable rate at which the file HANDOFF.md calls 'The authority' decays — six wrong counts in a document whose last self-dated edit is four days and 372 commits behind HEAD. The bridge-route count is the one with teeth: '28 for 100 backend routes' understates the coverage gap that AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md had to write a whole topology warning about.

priorFinding.note: The 2026-08-04 audit made the same observation ('CLAUDE.md is materially out of date: documents src/ as ~250 modules') — but its own replacement figures are stale too (it says 39 pages / 30 bridge routes / 82 routes; measured 41 / 36 / 99). Re-measured here rather than inherited.

whatWorks: Every one of the 52 file paths CLAUDE.md cites exists — 52/52, zero missing. The document's references are sound; its arithmetic is not. That is the cheapest possible thing to automate.
requiredRepair: Generate the Directory Structure counts in CI (six one-line shell commands) and fail the build when the file disagrees, or delete the counts. A number nobody can regenerate should not be in the authority document.

title: The two prior audits scope different objects and neither is wrong; the 08-04 audit's registry is 372 commits stale and at least one Critical finding was fixed 6h44m after the SHA it read
claimUnderTest: Two audits sit in docs/audits/ with nothing marking their relationship: 07-29 says 'Overall health: good, and better than the surrounding documentation suggested'; 08-04 says 'No — not at the decision layer ... Safe as a primary decision tool: 1'.
observed: HYPOTHESIS TESTED: they scope the value SPINE versus the DECISION LAYER on top of it. FALSIFICATION CONDITION declared in advance: false if (F1) they assert opposite verdicts about the same named artefact with no scope difference, or (F2) the 08-04 negative case rests materially on defects inside the spine. EVALUATION — F1 not met: the 08-04 audit's own §1 concedes the 07-29 object verbatim ('a genuinely well-built spine: one canonical value, one blend path, a correctly-reasoned scoring-profile/league-key split, a real and largely-held rule against a frontend ranking engine') and scopes its verdict in the sentence itself ('No — NOT AT THE DECISION LAYER'). Its own registry entry PRIOR-A11-F12 checked CLAUDE.md's pipeline stage by stage and returned 'CONFIRMED CORRECT' on twelve consecutive spine claims, at Informational severity. F2 not met: six of its seven systemic problems are located above the spine (labellers, engines, missing-data defaults, monitoring, documentation); only #2 touches it, and #2 is an argument about the BENCHMARK grading the curves — which is the 07-29 audit's own stated open question. HYPOTHESIS SURVIVES. The single genuine head-to-head — the trade finder — resolves on chronology, not scope: the 08-04 audit read 9c5d972f (2026-08-04 06:32 UTC) and commit a62af217 'Fix the arbitrage finder dropping every IDP asset' landed at 13:16 UTC, 6h44m later and NOT an ancestor of the audited SHA. At HEAD the claim is refuted by runtime.

reproduction.command: git merge-base --is-ancestor a62af217 9c5d972f; echo "exit=$? (1 = fix is NOT in the audited commit)"; git log -1 --format='%ad %s' --date=iso a62af217; git log --oneline 9c5d972f..e96c06ef | wc -l; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/finder -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"leagueKey":"dynasty_main","myTeam":"Jason","opponentTeams":["all"]}' | python3 -c "import sys,json,collections;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['metadata']['marketCoverage']);c=collections.Counter();[c.update([p['position']]) for t in d['trades'] for k in ('give','receive') for p in t.get(k,[]) if isinstance(p,dict) and p.get('position')];print(dict(c))"
reproduction.expected: if the 08-04 claim held at HEAD: no idpTradeCalc coverage and no IDP positions in trades
reproduction.actual: exit=1; a62af217 = 2026-08-04 13:16:03 +0000; 372 commits between; marketCoverage {'ktcSfTep':132,'ktc':18,'idpTradeCalc':150}; trades contain DL/DB/LB

numericProof.expected: < 0 if the audit saw the fix

userImpact: This is the finding that prevents wasted remediation. Without it a reader picks a winner between two correct audits, and either dismisses 173 open Critical/High decision-layer findings because 'the 07-29 audit said health is good', or re-fixes a trade-finder regression that was already fixed the same afternoon. The 08-04 registry's 531 findings are a claim set against a commit 372 behind HEAD, and the finder case proves at least one Critical entry was remediated in that window — in direct response to the audit.

priorFinding.note: My independent stage-by-stage pass over CLAUDE.md's Live Value Pipeline reached the same twelve verdicts as PRIOR-A11-F12 before I opened the index (constants, ordering, alpha, lambda, haircut, clamp scope, two-way ordering, Phase 3a/5.2b, weights all 1.0, default_weights unread). Separately REFUTES the 08-04 audit's problem-#4 finder claim at HEAD, and the refutation is chronological rather than a disagreement about facts.

whatWorks: Both audits are unusually good at their own object, and both were honest about limits — the 07-29 audit lists inherited claims it disproved rather than dropping them, and the 08-04 audit states outright that it could not run pytest. What is missing is one scope line and one commit stamp in each header.
rootCause: Two audits with different scopes filed to the same directory with no relationship metadata, and the newer one's SHA was not carried into its findings.
requiredRepair: Add to each header: the object audited (value spine / decision layer), the SHA, and a one-line pointer to the other. Stamp the 531-record registry with 9c5d972f and mark the finder finding superseded by a62af217.
dependencies: Every workstream assigning priorFinding.relation depends on this commit window being known.

title: 58 of 144 markdown documents are superseded, stale or self-declared untrustworthy, and only two of the 22 in docs/status/ say so
claimUnderTest: HANDOFF.md designates CLAUDE.md 'The authority' and the repo's own documented top failure mode is docs-drift. Implicit claim: the surrounding 143 documents are a usable corpus.
observed: 144 tracked markdown files outside node_modules/frontend/master-site-audit. Per-file disposition in supersession-list.csv: 81 KEEP, 48 ARCHIVE, 10 RETIRE, 5 REVIEW — 794,145 bytes (58 files) that should leave the working set. docs/status/ holds 22 files of which 20 have a latest internal date of 2026-04-28 or earlier and describe a pipeline retired at the 2026-04-20 Final Framework transition; exactly ONE carries a STALE banner and one 'superseded', so the other twenty read as current. UNIMPLEMENTED_BACKLOG.md (41,601 b) sits in the repo root beside CLAUDE.md with a header that says 'much of this file is already superseded' and 'the remaining entries were not re-verified one by one — treat them with the same suspicion', after two of its entries were found to be actively misreporting risk. docs/CLAUDE_SESSION_AUDIT_HANDOFF.md is 142,235 b — the largest document in the repo — and is a session-scoped handoff from 2026-07-31. Note git mtimes are useless for this: history was squashed on 2026-08-03, so every file shows the same date and only self-declared dates discriminate.

reproduction.command: git ls-files '*.md' | grep -v node_modules | grep -v ^frontend/ | grep -v ^docs/master-site-audit/ | wc -l; for f in docs/status/*.md; do printf '%s [%s] %s\n' "$(grep -ohE '20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' $f | sort | tail -1)" "$(grep -ohE 'STALE|superseded' $f | sort -u | tr '\n' ',')" "$f"; done | sort
reproduction.expected: a corpus whose staleness is visible from the file
reproduction.actual: 144 docs; 20 of 22 in docs/status/ are >=3 months stale with no marker

userImpact: This is the mechanism behind almost every other finding in this shard. A reader looking for the truth about the pipeline can land on docs/status/blueprint-source-of-truth.md (2026-03-14, no marker) or docs/BLUEPRINT_EXECUTION.md (STALE) and get a description of a system that was replaced four months ago, with no signal that anything is wrong. The repo's own 2026-08-04 audit named 'documentation mismatch' its single largest root-cause category; the corpus size is why.

priorFinding.note: The prior index carries individual doc-mismatch findings (82 records mention documentation or CLAUDE.md). None of them proposes a corpus-level disposition, which is what this audit needs in order to reduce the doc count rather than add to it.

whatWorks: The repo is unusually honest when it does mark staleness — UNIMPLEMENTED_BACKLOG.md's header, final-framework-transition.md's 'superseded', and the struck-through corrections inside the backlog are all better practice than most codebases manage. The failure is that the honesty is applied to 1 file in 10.
rootCause: No retirement step. Documents are added on completion and never removed, and the 2026-08-03 history squash destroyed the mtime signal that would otherwise expose age.
requiredRepair: Execute supersession-list.csv: move the 48 ARCHIVE files to docs/archive/<period>/ with one INDEX.md each, delete the 10 RETIRE files, triage the 5 REVIEW. Then add a rule to HANDOFF.md: a doc that is not linked from HANDOFF.md within one release is archived. Net effect of this audit becomes -58 documents rather than +1.
dependencies: Operator decision required before deleting anything; this shard proposes, it does not remove.
